review.body:
### Scope startup focus clearing to the initial activation path and guard XamlRoot nulls

**Severity:** high

Please scope the new focus redirect to the initial startup activation only, and return early when `XamlRoot` is null before touching `FocusManager`. The preview-size callback fires during later resize/navigation and can steal focus from interactive preview content if it keeps redirecting title-bar focus.

### Preserve interactive-preview keyboard navigation while handling Alt+Left/Alt+Right

**Severity:** medium

Please gate the low-level `VK_LEFT` and `VK_RIGHT` hook on `Alt` so ordinary arrow keys continue to reach WebView2 and other interactive preview controls. Keep the hidden focus sink out of normal tab navigation and add or retain focused UI coverage proving the title bar is not focused on startup and that Alt+Left/Alt+Right still changes the selected file while an interactive preview has focus.

proposed_comments.title: Scope startup focus clearing to the initial activation path and guard XamlRoot nulls
proposed_comments.body:
### Scope startup focus clearing to the initial activation path and guard XamlRoot nulls

**Severity:** high

**Affected code:** `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/PeekXAML/MainWindow.xaml.cs`, `FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged`, and `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/PeekXAML/Views/TitleBar.xaml.cs`.

**Problem:** The startup focus redirect can be triggered again when the preview size changes during later resize/navigation, and it also assumes the window has a connected `XamlRoot` before the first layout notification. That lets a non-startup preview-size callback steal focus from an interactive previewer or dereference a null root during early activation.

**Why it matters:** The window should only clear the default title-bar focus once when it is actually showing for startup, not on every later resize event. Failing to guard the lifecycle can steal keyboard focus away from WebView2 or other interactive preview content and makes the startup behavior nondeterministic before the window is fully connected.

**Suggested change:**
1. Move the initial focus cleanup behind a one-time startup guard that runs only after the window is visible and only when the actual title-bar button is focused.
2. Exit early if `XamlRoot` is null before calling `FocusManager` or any other root-dependent API.
3. Keep the redirect scoped to the initial activation path so later `PreviewSizeChanged` events cannot re-trigger focus theft.
4. Add a focused regression test that verifies the title-bar buttons do not take focus on startup and that a later resize/navigation event does not steal focus from an interactive preview.

**Verification:** Rebuild the exact upstream head and confirm the title bar starts unfocused while a preview is shown, and confirm resize/navigation events no longer steal focus from an interactive preview after the window has connected.

**Out-of-diff notes:** The fix requires a startup-only focus guard and a null-root guard in the live window lifecycle, and it is not safely expressible as a single inline suggestion on the current upstream diff.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve interactive-preview keyboard navigation while handling Alt+Left/Alt+Right
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve interactive-preview keyboard navigation while handling Alt+Left/Alt+Right

**Severity:** medium

**Affected code:** `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/PeekXAML/MainWindow.xaml.cs`, `FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged`, `FocusSink`, and `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/PeekXAML/Views/TitleBar.xaml.cs`.

**Problem:** The keyboard hook currently intercepts left/right navigation too broadly; when Alt is not pressed, normal arrow keys should keep flowing to interactive preview controls such as WebView2. At the same time, the hidden focus sink should not become part of normal tab order while the startup focus transfer is active.

**Why it matters:** Interactive previewers rely on arrows for their own controls, and a broad low-level hook can steal those keystrokes before the control receives them. This makes the Peek preview feel broken even though the file-change navigation is intended only for Alt+Left/Alt+Right.

**Suggested change:**
1. Gate the `VK_LEFT` and `VK_RIGHT` interception on `altPressed` so plain arrow keys continue to the active preview control.
2. Keep the hidden `FocusSink` non-tab-stop during normal keyboard navigation and enable it only briefly around the programmatic focus transfer.
3. Retain or add focused UI coverage proving the title-bar buttons are not focused on startup and that Alt+Left/Alt+Right still changes the selected file while an interactive preview has focus.

**Verification:** Rebuild the exact upstream head and run the Peek UI tests or a focused manual interaction test to confirm arrow keys still reach WebView2/interactive preview controls, while Alt+Left/Alt+Right changes the selected file only when the user is using the Peek navigation shortcut.
